description: German funding programmes with English translations for international users based in Germany

programmes.name_en: KfW Development Bank Loans – Digitalization & Innovation
programmes.summary_en: Long-term financing through Germany's development bank for digitalization and innovation projects, offered via commercial banks at reduced interest rates.
programmes.notes_en: Via commercial bank, long-term financing for digitalization projects

programmes.summary_en: Baden-Württemberg state grant for digitalization, AI implementation, and process optimization projects for companies located in the state.
programmes.notes_en: State program, for companies located in Baden-Württemberg

programmes.summary_en: Berlin's primary R&D and innovation funding program for technology-focused projects including AI and digitalization initiatives.
programmes.notes_en: Berlin-specific, for innovative R&D projects with technology focus

programmes.summary_en: Berlin grant supporting external business coaching for strategy, digitalization, and market entry for SMEs and freelancers.
programmes.notes_en: Supports external coaching for strategy, digitalization, market entry

programmes.summary_en: Berlin grant for technology transfer and collaborative projects with research institutions, including AI initiatives.
programmes.notes_en: Supports technology transfer; including AI projects with research partners

programmes.focus_en: External development services (e.g., prototyping, feasibility studies)
programmes.summary_en: Bavarian voucher program supporting external R&D services such as prototyping and feasibility studies for SMEs and craftsmen.
programmes.notes_en: Supports external R&D services; suitable for SMEs and craftsmen

programmes.focus_en: R&D projects, cooperation projects, innovation networks
programmes.summary_en: Federal innovation program for SMEs with R&D projects, cooperation initiatives, and innovation networks. High relevance for AI projects.
programmes.notes_en: For innovative SMEs with research and development projects

programmes.summary_en: Federal startup grant for technology-oriented and knowledge-based spin-offs from universities and research institutions.

programmes.focus_en: Administrative digitalization, IT security, process automation
programmes.summary_en: Various state-level programs for digitalization and IT security, with funding rates and focus areas varying by federal state.
programmes.notes_en: Funding rates and focus areas vary by federal state

programmes.max_amount_en: DFFF I up to €5m; DFFF II (VFX/production services) up to €25m
programmes.focus_en: Theatrical film production; digitalized production processes eligible
programmes.summary_en: Federal grant (BKM, administered by the FFA) reimbursing 30% of German production spend since the 2025 film law reform; rolling applications up to 6 weeks before principal photography. A merged DFFF/GMPF 'incentive funding' guideline was announced for mid-2026 — check ffa.de for the current state.
programmes.notes_en: FFG reform in force since 1 Jan 2025; higher caps (DFFF I €5m / DFFF II €25m)

programmes.focus_en: Levy-financed federal film funding via reference points; writers and directors now share in reference funds
programmes.summary_en: Since the 2025 film law reform the FFA's selective project funding (loans) was abolished; production funding now runs automatically via reference points earned through box-office, festival and award success.
programmes.notes_en: Selective project and distribution funding abolished as of 1 Jan 2025

programmes.max_amount_en: series up to €20m per season; non-theatrical films up to €5m
programmes.focus_en: High-end series and films with a high VFX/post-production share
programmes.summary_en: Guideline of the Federal Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM), administered by the FFA — relevant for high-end series and VFX/post-heavy productions; from 2026 a joint budget with the DFFF (approx. €250m/year).
programmes.notes_en: BKM programme (not BMWK); caps raised in 2025

programmes.max_amount_en: up to €8m per project (minimum project size €300k)
programmes.summary_en: Moved to the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) in May 2025 and reopened for applications in August 2025 after a multi-year freeze; 2026 budget €125m with substantial funds still available mid-2026. Applications via DLR project management agency; culture test and USK rating required.
programmes.notes_en: Reopened since 08/2025; good application prospects mid-2026

programmes.focus_en: Film, high-end series, new media/games, innovative audiovisual content
programmes.summary_en: Regional funder with a dedicated 'New Media' strand for innovative formats (XR, games, AI-assisted projects); regional spend required.

programmes.name_en: FFF Bavaria – Film and Television Fund
programmes.focus_en: Production, development, games, VFX; dedicated digital strands
programmes.summary_en: Bavaria's film fund with dedicated strands for games and VFX; regional spend required.

programmes.focus_en: Film, series, games, audio, innovative formats
programmes.summary_en: Broad regional funder including games and digital strands; regional spend required.

programmes.name_en: MFG Baden-Württemberg – Film and Media Fund
programmes.summary_en: Regional funder with an animation/VFX cluster focus (Ludwigsburg) and digital content strands.

programmes.name_en: Jury-Based Cultural Film Funding of the Federal Government
programmes.max_amount_en: treatment up to €15k, screenplay up to €40k, feature production up to €1m
programmes.focus_en: Culturally valuable film projects: treatment, screenplay, development, production, distribution
programmes.summary_en: BKM funds administered by the FFA since 1 Jan 2025 (guideline of 31 Mar 2025); screenplay/treatment funding is open to individual writers; fixed submission deadlines via the FFA service portal.
programmes.notes_en: Open to individual writers for screenplay/treatment funding

programmes.focus_en: Digitization of historically, artistically or documentarily valuable films
programmes.summary_en: Jointly financed by BKM, the federal states and the FFA; two annual deadlines (15 Jan and 15 Jul); open to rights holders and film heritage institutions — a good fit for archive digitization and AI-metadata monetization projects.
